title: BARCODE Efficiency Act
official_title: Barcode Automation for Revenue Collection to Organize Disbursement and Enhance Efficiency Act
summary: When taxpayers prepare their returns electronically but print and mail them, the IRS has to transcribe that data by hand to get it into electronic format. This bill requires those returns to be formatted so they are compatible with the IRS's scanning technology, and requires the IRS to use scanning technology to convert them automatically. For returns prepared entirely by hand and for paper correspondence, the IRS must use optical character recognition technology. The requirement can be waived if the Secretary of the Treasury determines it is slower or less reliable than manual processing — but any waiver must be reported to Congress within 30 days.
brief: Requires electronically-prepared paper tax returns to be formatted for the IRS's scanning technology, and mandates optical character recognition for handwritten returns and paper correspondence, with a performance-based waiver.

top_lines.headline: Scanning of E-Prepared Paper Returns
subs: E-prepared paper returns must be formatted for the IRS's scanning technology
Applies to individual income tax returns 180 days after enactment

top_lines.headline: OCR for Everything Else
subs: Hand-prepared returns and paper IRS correspondence transcribed via optical character recognition
Estate and gift returns: 24 months; all other returns and correspondence: 18 months after enactment

top_lines.headline: Performance Waiver
subs: IRS may skip the technology if it's slower or less reliable than manual processing — but must report to Congress within 30 days

likelihoodReason: Bipartisan sponsorship (Schneider D-IL and Yakym R-IN) and the efficiency framing make opposition difficult to articulate, but only 1 cosponsor. IRS technology mandate bills often face implementation feasibility questions in the Senate, particularly when they include performance-based exceptions that give the agency discretion to delay compliance.

items.main: Names the Act the “Barcode Automation for Revenue Collection to Organize Disbursement and Enhance Efficiency Act” (the “BARCODE Efficiency Act”).
items.detail: Short-title section — citation name only; no substantive effect.

sections.label: Section 2 — Scanning and Digitization of Tax Returns and Correspondence

items.main: Requires that any federal tax return prepared electronically and filed on paper be formatted in a manner compatible with the IRS's scanning technology, and that the IRS use that scanning technology to convert such returns to electronic format.
items.detail: If the data included in such a return cannot be accurately converted, the IRS must use optical character recognition or functionally similar technology. For paper returns not prepared electronically and all paper correspondence (except correspondence originally received electronically), the IRS must use OCR technology to transcribe the document. Effective dates key off January 1 of the first calendar year beginning more than a set period after enactment: 180 days for individual income tax returns, 18 months for all other returns and correspondence, and 24 months for estate and gift tax returns.

items.main: The technology requirement is waived if the Secretary determines it is slower or less reliable than manual transcription or any other IRS process — but a waiver report must be submitted to Congress within 30 days.
items.detail: The waiver determination is made entirely by the Secretary without independent oversight or minimum performance benchmarks. The reporting obligation to the Ways and Means Committee and Senate Finance Committee is the sole check on waiver use.

underreported.summary: The IRS determines whether its own technology is slower or less reliable than manual processing. If it makes that finding, it may waive the scanning and OCR requirements with no congressional approval required — only a 30-day report.
underreported.why_unreported: The bill's mandate reads as a firm requirement. The waiver mechanism allows the IRS to delay compliance through its own performance assessment, with a notification-only check. No minimum performance threshold, time limit on the waiver, or independent evaluation is specified.

featured_quotes.name: Mr. Yakym
featured_quotes.text: I am proud to co-lead this act with my friend from Illinois (Mr. Schneider). This is a simple but powerful bill that will make tax return processing faster, more accurate, and more efficient. E-filing taxes is becoming even more common. In 2009, two-thirds of taxpayers e-filed their returns. By 2015, it was up to 85 percent. Last year, 94 percent of taxpayers e-filed their returns. That remaining 6 percent still accounts for 10 million tax returns. There are good reasons to file a paper return.

gaps: The bill requires OCR for paper correspondence but does not address accuracy standards for the OCR process or what happens when digitized data contains errors that affect tax calculations or processing.

The bill does not specify what recourse taxpayers have if their paper-filed return is misread by the scanning technology or if the OCR transcription of their correspondence contains errors that affect their tax account.

added: Requirement that electronically-prepared federal tax returns filed on paper be formatted for compatibility with the IRS's scanning technology
Requirement for the IRS to use scanning technology to convert electronically-prepared paper returns to electronic format
Requirement for IRS to use optical character recognition technology for hand-prepared paper returns and paper correspondence

modified: Paper-printed e-prepared returns no longer must "bear a code which, when scanned" converts data — instead must be "formatted in a manner that is compatible with the scanning technology"
IRS conversion requirement generalized from "barcode scanning technology" to plain "scanning technology"
Effective date for other returns and correspondence delayed — now received on or after the first calendar year beginning more than 18 months after enactment (was 12 months)
